title.narrative: Integrated Humanitarian Response to Enhance Access to Basic Services for Vulnerable Returnees and Host Communities in Al Hasakeh, Aleppo, Daraa and Latakia

description.narrative: ltpgtSyria is facing an escalating humanitarian crisis, with 14.4 million people in urgent need of Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) assistance. This marks an increase since 2022 and reflects the deepening impact of systemic infrastructure collapse, chronic underfunding, economic decline, and environmental degradation. In Al-Hasakeh, the situation is especially dire due to the continued shutdown of the Allouk water station—once the region’s primary water source—leaving hundreds of thousands dependent on poor-quality wells and costly trucked water. Communities in Ras Al Ain, Tal Tamer, Markada, Al-Hasakeh city, and Al Hol are experiencing the highest levels of WASH vulnerability, exacerbated by drought, displacement, and a lack of coping mechanisms.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo address these intersecting needs, UNICEF is launching an integrated, multisectoral response that combines critical WASH interventions with life-saving Nutrition services, aimed at enhancing child and family wellbeing in both Al-Hasakeh and Aleppo governorates.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgt WASH:lt/bgtltbrgtThe project will focus on rehabilitating essential water infrastructure (Allouk Water Station) feeding water to eligible locations identified by the call for proposals (Ras Al Ain, Tal Tamer, and Markada). Due to the specificity and criticality of the water situation in Al-Hasakeh, the rehabilitation work will also benefit other communities in Al-Hasakeh such as (Al-Hasakeh City and Hole).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe rehabilitation works will target water wells, pumping facilities, pipelines, and distribution networks in Al-Hasakeh. The required rehabilitation work includes not only technical aspects but also high-level coordination and advocacy with all parties involved in Damascus and the Northeast. The required work to operate the station will be jointly coordinated and conducted with the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) with approximate funds of around US$ 2 million.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThese efforts are crucial in the upcoming winter to restore access to safe water for households, IDP communities, and service facilities, reducing reliance on humanitarian water trucking and the use of unsafe sources, and mitigating the spread of waterborne diseases such as Acute Watery Diarrhea (AWD) in the upcoming summer season. Improvements in WASH infrastructure and service delivery are essential to enabling the safe and effective delivery of nutrition services.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbgt Nutrition:lt/bgt In Aleppo, Lattakia, and Dara'a, a complementary cash-based nutrition program will support families with children aged 6–23 months through quarterly transfers of USD 150, alongside a package of preventive services including nutrient supplements, nutrition education, and early childhood development support (delivered through complementary resources). These interventions aim to reduce food poverty, enhance diet diversity, and build resilience among vulnerable households.lt/pgt
